newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QNI finalises revised Gencor deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QNI finalises revised Gencor deal.

text.p: Australian nickel producer QNI Ltd said on Tuesday it has reached a definitive agreement on its proposed merger with south Africa based miner Gencor Ltd's nickel business.
QNI said in a statement the deal has been found to be fair and reasonable by an independent expert's report.

Under the deal, QNI is to issue 455.8 million new shares to Gencor's base metals arm Billiton Plc, representing 52.5 percent of the enlargbed QNI. The capital return to shareholders would be 30 cents per share, compared with 28 cents previously.
The original merger proposal was for the issue of 504 million QNI shares to Gencor, which would have given the South African-based group a 55 percent stake in the enlarged group.
A further one percent of QNI was to have been issued to Gencor, subject to certain conditions, in relation to Billiton's Lake Johnston joint venture.
The merger to create one of the world's top five nickel groups was announced on June 18, but the deal, which needs shareholder approval, quickly ran into criticism.
QNI shares traded lower on concerns the merger would dilute earnings per share for at least two years.
QNI said changes to the original deal meant the sale and purchase agreement would be with Billiton, which had acquired Gencor's nickel division.

No further shares would be issued in relation to the acquisition of Billiton's interest in Lake Johnston, and the issue of the 455.8 million new shares would increase the total share capital to 862.2 million shares.
The proposed capital return to shareholders, through a reduction in the share premium reserve, would remain A$260 million and would amount to 30 cents a share.
It was expected to be paid in October.

QNI said the final merger ratio took into account finalisation of the accounts of the companies, the completion of detailed merger talks, and the impact of the movements in exchange rates since early June.

QNI managing director Wyn Davies said he was pleased the merger terms had been agreed. "Due diligence inquiries have served to reinforce our view of the quality of the assets which we are acquiring," he said in a statement.
Billiton nickel division chief executive Chris Pointon said he believed the two management teams would work well to unlock the growth potential of the combined businesses.
An explanatory memorandum and independent expert's report would be sent to shareholders on August 11.
An extraordinary general meeting for QNI shareholders to vote on the merger was expected on or about September 5.
QNI shares were 12 cents lower at A$2.38 at 10.40 a.m. (0040 GMT) after having been reinstated to trading after being suspended on July 30 pending today's announcement.
